name: Switzerland: the Oberland, Zermatt, the Engadin and Ticino

cities.base: The Altstadt between Bahnhofstrasse and the Niederdorf, or Kreis 4 and 5 if you want dinner under CHF 40. Everything central is walkable and the airport is 12 minutes by train from Hauptbahnhof.
cities.name: Zürich

cities.base: The old town on the north bank between the Kapellbrücke and the Museggmauer. Ten minutes on foot from the station, the boat pier and both covered bridges, and the steamers leave from the quay.
cities.name: Lucerne

cities.base: The valley floor at Lauterbrunnen if you want buses, trains and a car park, or Wengen and Mürren above it if you want quiet and no road at all. Wengen costs more and is closer to the Jungfrau trains.
cities.name: The Lauterbrunnen valley: Wengen and Mürren

cities.base: Anywhere within ten minutes of the Bahnhofstrasse, which is most of the village. Winkelmatten at the top end is quieter; the streets by the Gornergrat station suit catching first trains.
cities.name: Zermatt

cities.base: The old town inside the Aare loop, between the station and the Münster. The whole thing is arcaded, so rain does not decide your day, and nothing you want is more than fifteen minutes on foot.
cities.name: Bern

cities.base: The lakefront between the station and Territet, or Vevey four minutes along the shore, which is cheaper and has the better market. Both put the Lavaux path and Chillon twenty minutes away.
cities.name: Montreux and Vevey

cities.base: Around Piazza Riforma and the lakefront, or Paradiso at the foot of the San Salvatore funicular. The centre is small and steep, and the boats to Gandria and Morcote leave from the quay below the park.
cities.name: Lugano

cities.base: Pontresina rather than St. Moritz: the same trains and the same lifts, a third less per night and none of the attitude. It is five minutes from Punt Muragl and fifteen from Morteratsch and Diavolezza.
cities.name: Pontresina and the Upper Engadin

cities.base: There is nowhere to sleep at 3,454m except the research station. You sleep in Lauterbrunnen, Wengen or Grindelwald and take one of the first two trains, because the cloud builds by eleven.
cities.name: The Jungfraujoch

cities.base: Mürren has hotels and Gimmelwald has two hostels, and both are worth a night, but on a normal trip this is a day out of Lauterbrunnen. There is no road up, and the last cable car down is around 17:00.
cities.name: Mürren and the Schilthorn

cities.base: Only the Kulmhotel 3100 is up here, sold as a stargazing package rather than a base. You sleep in Zermatt, five minutes from the cog railway, and take the first train for the Riffelsee.
cities.name: The Gornergrat

cities.base: Riederalp and Bettmeralp have hotels and are right if you want two days on the ice. Otherwise it is a long day from Zermatt or a night in Fiesch, and the plateau shuts for six weeks each spring.
cities.name: Riederalp and the Aletsch glacier

cities.base: Two hotels on the summit and a few in Kaltbad, worth it only for the sunrise. Otherwise this is a day from Lucerne: paddle steamer to Vitznau, cog railway up, and down the far side to Arth-Goldau.
cities.name: The Rigi

cities.base: Andermatt has beds and is reasonable if you are driving the passes, but on a rail trip it is a change of train. The roads above it are shut by snow from late October to early June.
cities.name: Andermatt and the Furka pass

cities.base: Nothing at Ospizio Bernina or Alp Grüm but two restaurants and a platform reachable only by train. You sleep in Pontresina or St. Moritz and ride out; the line runs all year.
cities.name: The Bernina line: Ospizio and Alp Grüm

cities.base: The villages have a handful of rooms and Cully has more, but this is an afternoon from Montreux. Trains stop at Lutry, Cully, Épesses, Rivaz and St-Saphorin, so you can start anywhere.
cities.name: The Lavaux terraces

cities.base: Appenzell town and Wasserauen have beds and the Äscher has none. From Zürich it is two hours by train, so leave at seven or sleep in Appenzell if you want the lake to yourself.
cities.name: Appenzell and the Ebenalp

cities.base: Bellinzona has beds and Lavertezzo has almost none. From Lugano it is 25 minutes by train to the castles and another 40 by postbus up the valley, and the last bus back down the Verzasca is early.
cities.name: Bellinzona and the Val Verzasca

places.name: Grossmünster
places.note: Zwingli preached the Swiss Reformation from this pulpit in 1519, and the interior is bare because of it. The 187 steps up the Karlsturm cost CHF 5 and give the only high view over the old town and the lake.

places.name: Fraumünster
places.note: Five Chagall windows from 1970 in the choir and a Giacometti rosette in the north transept. CHF 5, twenty minutes, and the one thing in Zürich worth queueing for on a grey morning.

places.name: Swiss National Museum
places.note: The clearest account anywhere of how a federation of cantons that argued for six hundred years ended up one country. CHF 13, closed Mondays, and the 2016 extension is good building in its own right.

places.name: Kunsthaus Zürich
places.note: The largest Giacometti holding in the world, plus Hodler, Füssli and the Bührle collection in the 2021 Chipperfield wing, which the city is still arguing about because of how that collection was assembled. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Lindenhof
places.note: The Roman customs post and then the imperial palace stood on this gravel terrace above the Limmat. Now it is lime trees, outdoor chess and the best free view across to the Niederdorf.

places.name: Im Viadukt and the Markthalle
places.note: Thirty-six arches of an 1894 railway viaduct filled with small shops and food stalls. The Markthalle does cheese, bread and a lunch counter for a third of restaurant prices, and it is closed Sundays.

places.name: Seebad Utoquai
places.note: An 1890 wooden bathing pavilion on piles in the lake, CHF 8, open only from about mid-May to mid-September. The water reaches 22C in July and the whole city swims here after work.

places.name: Uetliberg and the Planetenweg
places.note: Twenty minutes on the S10 from Hauptbahnhof, then a level two-hour ridge path south to Felsenegg with the Alps on the skyline in clear air. Covered by a ZVV day ticket or the Swiss Travel Pass.

places.name: Zeughauskeller
places.note: A 1487 arsenal serving twenty kinds of sausage and a proper Zürcher Geschnetzeltes at long shared tables. Loud, full of visitors, and still the honest answer to what this food actually is. About CHF 32 a plate.

places.name: Kronenhalle
places.note: Chagall, Miró and Picasso on the walls of a dining room that has not changed since Zürich's bankers were the only people in it. CHF 80 to 110 a head with wine, and worth exactly one night.

places.name: Confiserie Sprüngli
places.note: Luxemburgerli downstairs and a first-floor cafe where the bill for a coffee and two macarons tells you exactly what country you are in. Closed Sundays.

places.name: Kapellbrücke
places.note: A 1333 covered timber bridge with 17th-century painted panels in the gables, two thirds of which burned in 1993 and are replacements. The most photographed object in the country and an eight-minute walk.

places.name: Museggmauer
places.note: Nine towers of the 1386 city wall, four of them open to climb, free, roughly April to early November. The Zytturm clock has struck one minute before every other clock in Lucerne since 1535.

places.name: Rosengart Collection
places.note: Angela Rosengart knew Picasso and bought directly from him, and the basement of 125 David Douglas Duncan photographs of him at home is the reason to come. The Klees upstairs are the best outside Bern.

places.name: Swiss Museum of Transport
places.note: Locomotives, a cut-away of the Gotthard tunnel and a hall of aircraft, CHF 35 with a 50% discount on the Swiss Travel Pass rather than free entry. The best rainy day in central Switzerland.

places.name: Lion Monument
places.note: Thorvaldsen's dying lion, cut into the cliff in 1821 for the Swiss Guards killed at the Tuileries. Mark Twain called it the saddest stone in the world and you will share it with four coach parties.

places.name: Gletschergarten
places.note: Potholes ground into sandstone by a glacier twenty thousand years ago, found in 1872 by a man digging a wine cellar, plus a Victorian mirror maze. Next door to the Lion and considerably better than it.

places.name: Wochenmarkt on the Reuss
places.note: Produce, alp cheese and bread along both quays on Tuesday and Saturday mornings until about 13:00. This is where you buy lunch instead of paying CHF 30 for it.

places.name: KKL Luzern
places.note: Jean Nouvel's 1998 concert hall, with a roof cantilevered 45 metres over the lake and one of the two or three best acoustics in Europe. The summer festival runs mid-August to mid-September; tickets from about CHF 40.

places.name: The Lake Lucerne paddle steamers
places.note: Five working steamers from the early 1900s run the lake as scheduled transport, three hours each way to Flüelen. Fully covered by the Swiss Travel Pass, which is the single biggest reason the pass pays here.

places.name: Wirtshaus Galliker
places.note: Four generations of one family doing Luzerner Chügelipastete, tripe and calf's head in a room that has resisted every trend since 1856. Closed Sundays and Mondays, and you have to book.

places.name: Rathaus Brauerei
places.note: House-brewed unfiltered lager under the arcades of the 1606 town hall, with tables out over the Reuss. About CHF 7 for a half litre, which in this country counts as cheap.

places.name: Staubbach Falls
places.note: Two hundred and ninety-seven metres in a single drop, with a tunnel path behind the water open roughly June to October. Byron thought it looked like the tail of a pale horse; in a dry August it nearly stops.

places.name: Trümmelbach Falls
places.note: Ten glacial cascades inside the mountain, reached by a tunnel lift, draining the Jungfrau ice at up to twenty thousand litres a second. CHF 14, open April to early November only, and you will get wet.

places.name: The valley floor to Stechelberg
places.note: Eight flat kilometres between vertical walls past most of the 72 waterfalls this valley claims. A bus runs back every half hour, and this is the right thing to do on a day the tops are in cloud.

places.name: Wengen
places.note: Car-free because there has never been a road, fourteen minutes up by cog railway, and the terrace above the valley is where the shape of the place makes sense. The Lauberhorn downhill comes through in mid-January.

places.name: Männlichen and the Royal Walk
places.note: Cable car from Wengen, then a level 4.3km panorama path to Kleine Scheidegg with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau in front of you the whole way. Lifts run mid-June to late October; 50% off with a Swiss Travel Pass.

places.name: Kleine Scheidegg
places.note: A railway junction directly under the Eiger north face and the interchange for everything in this region. The terrace charges CHF 9 for a coffee and people still sit there two hours watching for climbers.

places.name: The Eiger Trail
places.note: Six kilometres along the base of the north face from Eigergletscher station down to Alpiglen, about 600m of descent on good path, with rockfall audible above you most of the day. Snow-free late June to mid-October.

places.name: Schynige Platte
places.note: An 1893 cog railway to 1,967m, an alpine garden with about 650 species, and the start of the Faulhorn ridge. It runs only from roughly 1 June to 20 October; CHF 64 return, half that with a Swiss Travel Pass.

places.name: Bachalpsee from First
places.note: An hour of nearly flat gravel from the First gondola to a lake that mirrors the Schreckhorn when the wind drops. The easiest big-mountain walk in the Oberland, which is why it is crowded by ten.

places.name: Hotel Oberland
places.note: The valley's default dining room: rösti, fondue, schnitzel, about CHF 32 a plate, and food served until 21:30, which here counts as late. Book in July or eat at 18:00 with everyone else.

places.name: Horner Pub
places.note: The one late bar on the valley floor, full of season staff and climbers waiting on a weather window. CHF 8 a pint and the only thing open after ten.

places.name: The Jungfrau Railway
places.note: Nine kilometres bored inside the Eiger and Mönch between 1896 and 1912, still the highest railway in Europe. About CHF 240 return from Lauterbrunnen in summer, CHF 179 with a Swiss Travel Pass, CHF 120 with a Half Fare Card.

places.name: The Sphinx terrace
places.note: A lift through the rock to an observation deck with the 20km Aletsch on one side and, in clear air, the Black Forest on the other. At this altitude one flight of stairs will wind you.

places.name: The Ice Palace
places.note: Tunnels and carvings cut into the glacier about 20m below the surface, kept at -3C and genuinely slippery. Fifteen minutes, included in the ticket, and the only part of the complex that is not a shop.

places.name: The Plateau
places.note: A roped snowfield where you stand on the actual glacier with the Jungfrau above you. It shuts in wind, and the reflected light in July is strong enough to burn the underside of your chin.

places.name: The walk to the Mönchsjochhütte
places.note: Forty-five minutes each way on a marked track across the firn to a hut at 3,657m, and the only real walking at the Joch. The altitude makes it much harder than the distance suggests; shut in bad weather.

places.name: Piz Gloria, Schilthorn
places.note: A revolving restaurant at 2,970m and the On Her Majesty's Secret Service set they have never stopped selling. Roughly CHF 108 return from Stechelberg, half with a Swiss Travel Pass, and the cableway is being rebuilt in stages.

places.name: The Thrill Walk at Birg
places.note: Two hundred metres of steel grating, wire cage and glass floor bolted to the cliff below Birg station, included in the Schilthorn ticket. Short, faintly ridiculous, and genuinely unpleasant if exposure bothers you.

places.name: The Northface Trail
places.note: Four hours of contour path from Allmendhubel round to Gimmelwald, facing the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau for most of it, with about 400m of climbing. Clear of snow from roughly mid-June. The Allmendhubel funicular is shut until 11 Dec 2026, so start on foot from Mürren.

places.name: Mürren and the Allmendhubel funicular
places.note: Car-free, one street long, with the three faces straight across the valley. The 1912 funicular to Allmendhubel is CHF 16 return, shut for revision until 11 Dec 2026 and again 5 April to 28 May 2027.

places.name: Gimmelwald
places.note: Twenty-odd farmhouses on a shelf below Mürren, no road, an honesty shop and a cheese cellar. It is what Mürren was before the cable car, and it is a 45-minute walk down from it.

places.name: The 5-Seenweg from Blauherd
places.note: Nine and a half kilometres and 400m down past Stellisee, Grindjisee, Grünsee, Moosjisee and Leisee, two of which hold the Matterhorn reflection. The Swiss Travel Pass discount does not apply on this side of the valley.

places.name: The Höhbalmen and Trift loop
places.note: Seven hours and 1,250m of climbing from the village to a meadow terrace at 2,700m under the Matterhorn's north face, out by the Trift gorge and back through Zmutt. The best hard day here and almost nobody on it.

places.name: Zmutt
places.note: A hamlet of stone and larch barns 90 minutes' walk west of Zermatt, with two kitchens doing dried meat, soup and rösti for about CHF 32. The easiest half day in the valley and the walk back is downhill.

places.name: Matterhorn Museum Zermatlantis
places.note: Built underground as a reconstructed village, around the broken rope from the 1865 first ascent on which four men died. CHF 12, well done, and the only indoor hour in Zermatt worth paying for.

places.name: The mountaineers' cemetery
places.note: The graves of climbers killed on the Matterhorn and Monte Rosa, some of them very young and some of them from this decade. It takes ten minutes and it undoes the gift-shop version of this place. Free and open all hours.

places.name: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise
places.note: The highest cable car station in Europe, with an ice palace inside the glacier and a view over into Italy. CHF 132 in peak season and half that with a Swiss Travel Pass; you gain 2,300m in forty minutes and people feel it.

places.name: The Gorner gorge
places.note: Wooden galleries bolted into a serpentine slot the Gornervispe has cut below the village. CHF 6, open roughly mid-June to mid-October, twenty minutes of actual gorge. Listed as temporarily closed in October 2026 with no reopening date, check.

places.name: Chez Vrony
places.note: A working farm above Findeln turned into the most booked lunch in the Alps, with the Matterhorn framed from every table. CHF 60 to 80 a head, reserve weeks out, and walk down afterwards rather than buying a lift ticket.

places.name: The Hörnlihütte path
places.note: From Schwarzsee up the Hörnli ridge to the climbers' hut at 3,260m, about 900m of ascent with cable-protected rock near the top. This is where the ordinary route on the Matterhorn starts and where walking stops.

places.name: Bahnhofstrasse
places.note: Electric taxis, watch shops and CHF 9 beers along one street. Worth a single evening walk to see how a farming village of 1850 monetised a mountain, and not worth a second.

places.name: Papperla Pub
places.note: The room under Hotel Julen where the season staff drink, CHF 9 a beer, loud from four in the afternoon all winter. Dead in the shoulder weeks, when half of Zermatt is closed anyway.

places.name: The Gornergrat
places.note: Thirty-three minutes up the 1898 cog railway, with the Matterhorn on one side and the Gorner glacier and Monte Rosa on the other. CHF 132 return in summer, CHF 96 in winter, half either way with a Swiss Travel Pass.

places.name: The Riffelsee
places.note: Ten minutes below Rotenboden station, and the pool that gives the reflected Matterhorn photograph. Take the first train: the wind gets up by nine and the reflection goes with it.

places.name: Riffelberg down to Zermatt on foot
places.note: Ride up and walk down: about 1,100m of descent through larch from Riffelberg to Zermatt in three hours, on wide path with the Matterhorn ahead the whole way. Saves half the fare and wrecks your knees.

places.name: The Gorner glacier viewpoint
places.note: Two minutes behind the terrace and away from the crowd, where the whole Gorner and Grenz glacier system runs south to Monte Rosa. It has lost well over a kilometre since the railway was built.

places.name: The Kulmhotel 3100 terrace
places.note: Europe's highest hotel, and a terrace where CHF 6 for a coffee is defensible because you are sitting at 3,100m in front of twenty-nine four-thousand-metre peaks.

places.name: The Eggishorn
places.note: The one place the whole 20km Aletsch is visible at once, right down to the bend at Konkordiaplatz. About CHF 56 return from Fiesch, half with a Swiss Travel Pass, and the last cable car down is earlier than you think.

places.name: Bettmerhorn and the glacier exhibition
places.note: A station built into the ridge with a free exhibition on how much ice this glacier has lost since 1850, which is about three kilometres of length. The terrace is the easiest close view of the ice.

places.name: Moosfluh to Bettmerhorn on the ridge
places.note: Seven kilometres of mostly level path at 2,300m along the lip of the ice. The slope here is visibly sliding as the glacier thins, and sections of the trail get rerouted most summers.

places.name: The Aletschwald
places.note: Eight-hundred-year-old Arolla pines on the slope above the glacier's south flank, protected since 1933 and reached on a level path from Riederfurka. The quietest three hours in the Valais.

places.name: Villa Cassel and the Pro Natura centre
places.note: An English banker's 1902 summer house on the Riederfurka where Churchill stayed as a young man, now a nature centre with an alpine garden. Open roughly mid-June to mid-October only.

places.name: Riederalp
places.note: A car-free village reached only by cable car from Mörel, where the groceries arrive by lift and the hotels close for six weeks in spring and again in November. The practical base for two days on the ice.

places.name: Rigi Kulm
places.note: Thirteen lakes and a third of the Alps from one summit, and the reason Europe built its first mountain railway here in 1871. CHF 78 return from Vitznau and fully covered by the Swiss Travel Pass, which is unusual.

places.name: The Rigi sunrise
places.note: What Turner and Mark Twain came up here for. You either sleep on the mountain or take the first train out of Vitznau in summer, and roughly half the time the whole thing is inside a cloud.

places.name: Rigi Kaltbad mineral baths
places.note: Mario Botta's 2012 bath house on a shelf at 1,450m, CHF 35 for three hours, with the outdoor pool facing down the lake. The correct thing to do on an afternoon the summit is in fog.

places.name: The Rigi panorama path
places.note: A nearly level two-hour path cut round the west face at 1,500m, with the Bernese Alps opposite and the lake 1,200m below. Snow-free roughly May to November and flat enough for a pushchair.

places.name: The Schöllenen gorge and the Devil's Bridge
places.note: The granite slot that made the Gotthard route possible and kept it shut until the 13th century. Three bridges from three centuries stand above each other and the 1799 Suvorov monument is cut into the rock.

places.name: The Furka pass
places.note: Two thousand four hundred and twenty-nine metres, the road from Goldfinger, and closed by snow from roughly late October to early June every year. The only winter workaround is the car train through the tunnel below.

places.name: The Rhône glacier ice grotto
places.note: A tunnel cut fresh into the ice each summer, CHF 10, open roughly June to October. The glacier has retreated so far from the 1856 hotel built to view it that reaching the ice is now a ten-minute walk down.

places.name: The Furka steam railway
places.note: Volunteers rebuilt the abandoned Furka summit line and run rack steam over the pass from Realp to Oberwald, about CHF 92 one way. It operates only from late June to early October, mostly at weekends, and books out.

places.name: The Oberalp pass and the source of the Rhine
places.note: The Rhine rises 400m above this pass at Lai da Tuma, and the four-source route starts here. Five hours return on marked path, with snow lingering into late June; the road shuts to cars in winter while the train keeps going.

places.name: The Tremola road over the Gotthard
places.note: Twenty-four cobbled hairpins on the south side of the pass, built in 1830 and left as they were when the motorway tunnel opened. Open roughly June to October, rough on a car, and the best drive in the country.

places.name: Zytglogge
places.note: The 13th-century clock tower, with an astronomical dial and a figure show four minutes before every hour. The CHF 16 tour of the 1530 movement is far better than standing in the street watching the puppets.

places.name: Bern Münster and the tower
places.note: Switzerland's tallest spire at 100.6m, finished in 1893 after 472 years of building, above a Last Judgment portal that survived the Reformation intact. CHF 5 and 344 steps for the platform.

places.name: The Lauben arcades and the fountains
places.note: Six kilometres of covered sandstone arcade, the longest in Europe, and eleven 16th-century fountains including one of a giant eating children. It makes the old town usable in rain, which Bern gets plenty of.

places.name: Zentrum Paul Klee
places.note: Four thousand Klees, of which about 120 hang at a time, inside three steel waves by Renzo Piano on the edge of town. CHF 24, closed Mondays, fifteen minutes by bus 12 from the station.

places.name: Kunstmuseum Bern
places.note: The oldest art museum in the country, strong on Hodler and Anker, and holder of the Gurlitt bequest which it spent years publicly investigating rather than quietly absorbing. CHF 20, closed Mondays.

places.name: The Bundeshaus
places.note: The federal parliament, free to tour when the chambers are not sitting, bookable in advance and with passport checks at the door. The dome mosaic reads one for all, all for one.

places.name: The Bear Park
places.note: Three brown bears on a wooded slope down to the Aare, which replaced the concrete pit in 2009 after a century of complaints. The city is named for them, it is free, and it takes half an hour.

places.name: The Aare swim, Eichholz to Marzili
places.note: Bernese people get in upstream and let a fast current carry them back into the city, June to early September. It is genuinely dangerous if you cannot pull yourself out at the ladders, and locals will say so.

places.name: The Rosengarten
places.note: A former cemetery on the hill across the Aare loop, 220 rose varieties, and the postcard view back over the roofs. Free, ten minutes uphill from the bear park, best an hour before sunset.

places.name: The Bundesplatz and Bärenplatz market
places.note: Tuesday and Saturday mornings on the square in front of parliament: Emmental cheese, Bernese bread and flower stalls spilling into Bärenplatz. Buy lunch here and it costs CHF 12 instead of CHF 35.

places.name: Kornhauskeller
places.note: A vaulted 1718 grain store with a painted ceiling, doing a decent modern Swiss menu at about CHF 55 a course. Go for the room rather than the cooking, and sit under the frescoes.

places.name: Restaurant Lötschberg AOC
places.note: A hundred Swiss wines by the glass and raclette from three different cheeses, about CHF 45 a head. Closed Sundays, and one of the few places in the country to drink Swiss wine at a sane markup.

places.name: Château de Chillon
places.note: A 12th-century Savoyard water castle on a rock in the lake, with the dungeon Byron wrote about and his name supposedly carved on a pillar. CHF 14.50, covered by the Swiss Travel Pass, and empty at opening.

places.name: The Montreux lake promenade
places.note: Seven kilometres of planted quay from Villeneuve to Vevey, with palms, cedars and sequoias that survive on the lake's microclimate. Flat, free, and the best thing in Montreux.

places.name: The Montreux Jazz Festival
places.note: Sixteen days in early July since 1967, with paid headline shows in the Stravinski hall and a lot of free music on the quays. Beds in Montreux roughly double for it and book out months ahead.

places.name: Rochers-de-Naye
places.note: Fifty-five minutes by cog railway from Montreux station to 2,042m, with an alpine garden, marmots and the whole lake below. About CHF 64 return, half with a Swiss Travel Pass, and often in cloud when the shore is clear.

places.name: Chaplin's World
places.note: Chaplin's actual house above Vevey, where he lived his last 25 years, plus a studio building of reconstructed sets. CHF 29, not covered by any rail pass, and better than it sounds if you care about the films.

places.name: Alimentarium, Vevey
places.note: Nestlé's museum of food in the town it comes from, more honest about industrial food than you would expect, with a working kitchen. CHF 13, closed Mondays, and the Vevey market is 200m along the quay.

places.name: The Vevey Saturday market
places.note: Grande Place fills with Vaud producers on Saturday mornings, and from July to September there is a folk market where you buy an empty glass for a few francs and fill it with Chasselas from the stalls.

places.name: The CGN Belle Époque steamers
places.note: Eight restored paddle steamers from between 1904 and 1927 still work Lac Léman as scheduled boats, and the Montreux to Chillon to Lausanne run is covered by the Swiss Travel Pass. Slow, which is the point.

places.name: Café du Grütli
places.note: Filets de perche from the lake, papet vaudois in winter, and a Vaud wine list, at about CHF 40 a plate, which is the going rate on this shore. A room of locals rather than conference guests. Closed Sundays.

places.name: The Lavaux terrace walk, Lutry to St-Saphorin
places.note: Eleven kilometres of path between the vines, UNESCO-listed since 2007, with the lake and the Savoy Alps below you the whole way. About 250m of up and down, trains back from every village, and no shade at all.

places.name: Lavaux Vinorama
places.note: Two hundred and ninety wines from eight kilometres of coast, tasted three at a time for about CHF 15, in a concrete room built into the hillside. Closed Mondays, and the Dézaley Chasselas is the one to try.

places.name: The Dézaley
places.note: The steepest and most expensive grand cru on the lake, terraced by Cistercian monks in the 12th century and held up by walls still repaired by hand. The path in from Épesses is where the view is.

places.name: Caveau des Vignerons, Épesses
places.note: A growers' cellar where one member pours their own bottles, open Thursday, Friday and Saturday evenings in season only. About CHF 4 a glass, cash, and they shut when the harvest starts.

places.name: Parco Ciani and the lakefront
places.note: A botanical park on a point in the lake with magnolias and cedars, free and open until dark, and the best thing in Lugano. The promenade runs three kilometres west to Paradiso from here.

places.name: LAC Lugano Arte e Cultura
places.note: Ivano Gianola's 2015 arts centre holding the cantonal collection and a concert hall. CHF 15, closed Mondays, and the Klee and Hodler rooms upstairs are better than the building's local reputation.

places.name: Monte Brè
places.note: Funicular from Cassarate to 925m on what is claimed as the sunniest slope in Switzerland, with a path down through Brè village and its sculpture trail. About CHF 30 return, half with a Swiss Travel Pass.

places.name: Monte San Salvatore
places.note: The better of the two mountains: funicular from Paradiso, a chapel on the summit rock, and a two-hour path down to Morcote through chestnut wood. The funicular runs mid-March to early November only.

places.name: Gandria and the olive path
places.note: A village of stacked houses with no road through it, reached by boat or by the Sentiero dell'Olivo, an hour of level shore path with signs about an olive industry that actually died out here around 1700.

places.name: Morcote and Parco Scherrer
places.note: Arcaded houses at the end of the peninsula, 404 steps up to Santa Maria del Sasso, and a 1930s merchant's garden full of Egyptian and Siamese follies. The garden opens mid-March to early November.

places.name: The Lugano market
places.note: Tuesday and Friday mornings in Piazza Riforma and the lanes behind it: Ticino cheese, cured meat and the first cherries in May. Southern Switzerland at its least Swiss.

places.name: Grotto Morchino
places.note: A grotto is a stone tavern in the chestnut wood, and this one does risotto, brasato and polenta at granite tables for about CHF 45. Merlot comes in a ceramic boccalino and the terrace only works in summer. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Bottegone del Vino
places.note: A wine bar behind Piazza Riforma pouring Ticino Merlot by the glass to the people who work in the banks upstairs. CHF 7 to 12 a glass and the food is a proper meal if you want it. Closed Sundays.

places.name: Castelgrande
places.note: The lowest and largest of the three castles, on a rock in the middle of the valley, reworked by Aurelio Galfetti in the 1980s in a way now studied as much as the medieval walls. CHF 10 covers all three.

places.name: Castello di Montebello
places.note: The middle castle, 90m above Castelgrande, with a dry moat and a drawbridge and the clearest view of the Murata, the wall the Milanese threw across the whole valley in 1487 to stop the Swiss.

places.name: Castello di Sasso Corbaro
places.note: Built in six months in 1479 after the Swiss won at Giornico, 230m above the town, reached by a stiff 45-minute walk or a short bus. The least visited of the three and the one with a courtyard worth sitting in.

places.name: The Ponte dei Salti at Lavertezzo
places.note: A 17th-century double-arched stone bridge over granite pools in the clearest river in the Alps. The water is about 10C in August, the rock is slippery, and people are killed here jumping most summers.

places.name: Corippo
places.note: Switzerland's smallest municipality until 2022, with about a dozen residents and a terrace of stone houses under slab roofs. It is being turned into a hotel village to keep it standing, which is either rescue or taxidermy.

places.name: The Verzasca dam
places.note: The 220m wall GoldenEye opens on, and still the highest commercial bungee jump in Europe at around CHF 255. Walking across it is free and takes five minutes; the jump runs roughly April to October.

places.name: The Morteratsch glacier trail
places.note: A level three kilometres from the railway halt to the ice, with year-markers along the path: 1878 is at the station and the snout is now about two kilometres further up. The clearest lesson in glacier retreat in the country.

places.name: Diavolezza
places.note: Cable car to 2,973m facing Piz Bernina and the Biancograt, the only four-thousand-metre peak in the eastern Alps. About CHF 35 return, half with a Swiss Travel Pass; the glacier crossing to Boval needs a guide and a rope.

places.name: Val Roseg
places.note: Two hours up an almost flat forest valley from Pontresina to a hotel, a milky glacier lake and the Roseg icefall. Horse carriages run it in summer and cross-country tracks in winter; the easiest big view in the Engadin.

places.name: Muottas Muragl
places.note: A 1907 funicular to 2,456m with the whole chain of Engadin lakes below and the best sunset terrace in the valley. About CHF 35 return, half with a Swiss Travel Pass, and the last car down is late enough to eat up there.

places.name: Segantini Museum, St. Moritz
places.note: The Alpine triptych Segantini painted for a pavilion that was never built, in a stone rotunda above St. Moritz. CHF 15, Tuesday to Sunday 11:00 to 17:00, and shut in the off-season weeks, so check.

places.name: The Nietzsche House, Sils Maria
places.note: The bare room Nietzsche rented for seven summers from 1881 and wrote most of Zarathustra in. Afternoons only, roughly mid-June to mid-October and again in winter, closed Mondays, and it takes forty minutes.

places.name: The Sils and Silvaplana lake path
places.note: A flat eight kilometres along the north shore past the Chastè peninsula, where the Nietzsche stone is. The Maloja wind gets up after midday and turns this water into the best kitesurfing in the Alps.

places.name: The Swiss National Park, Val Trupchun
places.note: The only national park in the country, founded 1914, where you may not leave the path, light a fire or bring a dog. Val Trupchun in late September holds the largest red deer rut in the Alps; shut by snow November to May.

places.name: Colani Stübli
places.note: Capuns, pizzoccheri and Engadin barley soup in a panelled room, about CHF 50 a head. This is where the local food actually is, rather than in the hotel dining rooms of St. Moritz.

places.name: Confiserie Hanselmann
places.note: An 1894 sgraffito-fronted cafe where the Engadiner Nusstorte is made properly and a slice with coffee runs to about CHF 13. The upstairs room is full of people who have been coming for forty years.

places.name: Alp Grüm
places.note: A station you can only reach by train, on the Italian side of the pass, looking straight down the Palü glacier into the Valtellina. The terrace restaurant is why people break the journey here.

places.name: Ospizio Bernina and Lago Bianco
places.note: The highest point of the line, on the watershed between the Danube and the Po, with a milky reservoir on one side and a dark lake on the other. It is bleak and it is the best part of the ride.

places.name: The Brusio circular viaduct
places.note: A spiral stone viaduct built in 1908 to lose height without a rack rail, and the picture on every poster for this railway. You see it properly from the road below rather than from the train.

places.name: The Bernina line to Tirano
places.note: Two thousand two hundred and fifty-three metres crossed without a rack rail, UNESCO-listed, ending in Italy. Ordinary regional trains are covered by the Swiss Travel Pass; the panoramic Bernina Express adds a reservation and does not open its windows.

places.name: Ebenalp and the Wildkirchli caves
places.note: Cable car from Wasserauen to 1,640m, then down through a cave system inhabited 40,000 years ago to a hermitage chapel cut into the rock. About CHF 37 return, half with a Swiss Travel Pass.

places.name: Berggasthaus Äscher
places.note: The inn built against the cliff that National Geographic put on a cover, serving walkers since 1846 and now turning away hundreds a day. CHF 25 for cheese, bread and rösti, and there is no road and no mains water.

places.name: The Seealpsee
places.note: An hour and a quarter up a farm road from Wasserauen to a lake under the Säntis wall, or ninety minutes across from Ebenalp. Two dairies sell their own cheese, and by eleven on a July Sunday it is full.

places.name: Appenzell village
places.note: Painted gable houses along the Hauptgasse in a half-canton where women could not vote on local matters until a federal court forced it in 1990. The Landsgemeinde still votes by show of hands in the square each April.

places.name: The Appenzeller Schaukäserei at Stein
places.note: A working dairy that makes the herb-washed Appenzeller in front of you and still will not say what is in the brine. CHF 12, and the restaurant does a cheese lunch at better value than anything in Appenzell town.

places.name: Mount Titlis
places.note: CHF 96 return from Engelberg for a rotating gondola, a cliff walk and a glacier cave, all of it queued and built over. Pilatus and the Rigi cost less, are covered better by the pass, and are better mountains.

places.name: Interlaken
places.note: Two lakes you cannot see from the middle of town, a paragliding landing field, and a main street of watch shops. Change trains here and sleep in the valley; there is nothing in Interlaken you came for.

places.name: Lindt Swiss Chocolate Heaven
places.note: A chocolate-themed walkthrough and shop inside the terminal. You have paid about CHF 240 to stand on a glacier at 3,454m; do not spend twenty minutes of that in a gift shop.

places.name: Bond World 007
places.note: An interactive exhibition at the summit station about a film shot here in 1969, no charge beyond the Schilthorn ticket. Ten minutes is plenty; the reason you are at 2,970m is on the other side of the window.

places.name: The Freddie Mercury statue
places.note: A three-metre bronze on the quay with a permanent queue of people doing the pose. Thirty seconds in passing; the Queen Studio Experience inside the Casino is the part actually worth paying for.

places.name: Haus Hiltl
places.note: Pay-by-weight buffet at CHF 5.90 per 100 g, or CHF 63 all you can eat, plus a carte of Thai, Indian and Swiss dishes at CHF 27 to 38. Order the Züri Geschnetzeltes, CHF 36. Open to 23:00 Thursday to Saturday, from 08:00 Saturday and 10:00 Sunday.

places.name: Swiss Chuchi (Hotel Adler)
places.note: The Hotel Adler's fondue room on Rosengasse: Moitié-Moitié fondue CHF 34.50 a head, raclette CHF 34.50 per 180 g, Älplermagronen CHF 25.50. Kitchen open to 23:15 every day, from 12:00 at weekends.

places.name: Old Swiss House
places.note: The show here is the Wiener Schnitzel finished at your table, CHF 66. Mains run CHF 51 to 69, every guest orders one, no sharing, and it is closed Sunday and Monday. Lunch 11:30 to 14:30, dinner from 18:00, book for dinner.

places.name: Wirtshaus Taube
places.note: Old-town Wirtshaus with a 2026 game card: Hirschschnitzel CHF 36.50, Wildbratwurst CHF 38.50, Äuplermagrone CHF 28.50. Open daily, but Tuesday is lunch only, to 14:30. Specialities week 2 to 9 November 2026.

places.name: Jesuit Church
places.note: The first large Baroque church in Switzerland north of the Alps, begun 1666 or 1667, consecrated 1677, the onion towers finished in 1893. Free. Thirty minutes for the stucco and high altar; Monday and Thursday it opens at 09:30.

places.name: Pasta & More, Wengen
places.note: Classic cheese fondue CHF 31 a head, Ticino fondue CHF 32, pasta CHF 26 to 37 and burgers CHF 27 to 35. Kitchen 12:00 to 21:30 daily. Prices are from the summer 2026 card, and the winter card may differ.

places.name: Restaurant Weidstübli
places.note: Closed for holidays until 18 December 2026. Then closed Monday and Tuesday, from 15:00 Wednesday and Thursday. Cheese fondue CHF 27, raclette CHF 22, Lauterbrunnen Rösti CHF 25, trout CHF 38.

places.name: Ristorante Da Sina, Wengen
places.note: Family-run Italian in Wengen, open daily 11:30 to 14:00 and 17:30 to 21:00. Penne alla Mamma CHF 25, pizza Margherita from CHF 16, cheese fondue CHF 35 a head for two or more. Prices from the summer 2025 menu.

places.name: Tal & Sagen Museum Lauterbrunnen
places.note: A former 16th-century mill holding the valley's bobbin lace, alpine cooking, ski collection and lead and lime mining. CHF 7, free with the guest card. Open mid-June to mid-October only, Tuesday and Thursday to Sunday.

places.name: Flower Trail, Allmendhubel
places.note: A short easy loop round Allmendhubel with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau across the valley, flowers best June to August. Free, but the funicular is shut until 11 Dec 2026, so walk up from Mürren.

places.name: Restaurant Schäferstube (Hotel Julen)
places.note: Lamb off a wood-fired grill, CHF 36 for the burger to CHF 41 for the leg, or fondue Maison at CHF 35 a head. Dinner only, daily, two seatings at 18:30 and 20:45, so book.

places.name: Pfarrkirche St. Mauritius
places.note: The parish church next to the Matterhorn Museum, with Baroque-style altars and a Noah's Ark ceiling fresco, and the mountaineers' cemetery outside. Hours and any charge are not listed, check.

places.name: Altes Tramdepot Brauerei Restaurant
places.note: Brewery restaurant above the Bear Park with the Old Town view. Cordon Bleu CHF 38, Rösti from CHF 24, bratwurst from CHF 26, a 3 dl Tram-Helles CHF 5.50. Open daily 11:00 to 23:30, with a weekly lunch menu.
places.neighborhood: Grosser Muristalden, above the Bear Park

places.name: Restaurant Le Museum
places.note: Dinner only, from 17:30 daily. Fondue moitié-moitié CHF 28 a head, Léman perch fillets CHF 48, and in autumn La Chasse, a game tasting menu at CHF 97.

places.name: Restaurant L'Armailli, Vevey
places.note: Pizzas made with alpine cheese, plus fondue: Napolitaine CHF 21, Maison CHF 18, lasagne CHF 24. Closed Sunday and Monday, shut 14:30 to 18:00, Saturday from 09:00. Prices from a December 2025 menu with no fondue price on it.
places.neighborhood: Vevey old town, Rue des Deux-Marchés

places.name: Musée Jenisch Vevey
places.note: Vevey's art museum, CHF 12, free the first weekend of the month, to 20:00 on Thursday event nights. Closed Monday, and shut 5 October to 4 November 2026 for an exhibition change, reopening 5 November.

places.name: Swiss Camera Museum, Vevey
places.note: The history of photography and cameras, French labels with English listening devices. Tuesday to Sunday 11:00 to 17:30. Free the first weekend of the month, otherwise check the price.

places.name: Musée historique de Vevey
places.note: Vevey's history in a 16th-century mansion: the Fête des Vignerons, archaeology, medieval objects, paintings and posters. Tuesday to Sunday 11:00 to 17:00. Free the first weekend of the month, otherwise check the price.

places.name: Ristorante della Torre, Morcote
places.note: Lake terrace in Morcote, 10 km south of Lugano by road or by boat in season. Risotto CHF 29 to 30, Wiener Schnitzel CHF 36, fish CHF 36 to 59. Daily, lunch 11:30 to 14:30, dinner 18:30 to 21:00.

places.name: Osteria Trani
places.note: Old-town osteria on Via Cattedrale: gnocchi CHF 29, risotto CHF 34, veal cheek CHF 42. Lunch 11:45 to 14:00 and dinner 18:45 to midnight, Saturday dinner only, closed Sunday.

places.name: Grand Café Al Porto
places.note: A lunch, not a dinner: open 08:00 to 18:30, food to 14:30, closed Sunday and holidays. Game ragù tagliatelle CHF 26, braised beef with polenta CHF 39 on the late-October card, which changes monthly.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria degli Angioli
places.note: Former Franciscan church with Bernardino Luini's 1529 Passion fresco across the whole dividing wall, and his Last Supper. Open 08:30 to 18:00, no admission price listed, check the price. Masses and concerts at weekends.

places.name: Swissminiatur, Melide
places.note: Open since 1959: 128 models of Swiss landmarks, Chillon and the Bundeshaus among them, plus model trains, on 14,000 m2. 09:00 to 18:00, check the price and the season, which runs at least to 8 November.

places.name: Museo Hermann Hesse Montagnola
places.note: Hesse lived in Montagnola for 43 years, until his death in 1962. CHF 10, 10:30 to 17:30, about 6 km from Lugano, with a walking route on his footsteps. Closed 1 November 2026 to 26 March 2027.

places.name: Pizzeria Ristorante Riccardo's
places.note: Spätzle, risotto and pizza, kitchen to 21:30 and pizzas to 22:00. The weekday lunch plate is CHF 16, or CHF 22 with salad, 11:45 to 13:45. A la carte prices are not published, so budget more for dinner.

places.name: La Trattoria (Hotel Walther)
places.note: Evenings only, seatings 18:00 and 20:15, closing time not published. Saltimbocca CHF 48, lasagne CHF 28. Thursday to Sunday to 1 Nov, Thursday to Saturday 5 Nov to 9 Dec 2026, then Thursday to Monday from 11 Dec.

places.name: Museum Alpin Pontresina
places.note: Grisons wildlife and geology and the history of the SAC huts, in Chesa Delnon, a 1716 Engadine house. CHF 9, free with the Swiss Museum Pass. Monday to Saturday 15:30 to 18:00 from one listing only, so check.

places.name: Engadiner Museum, St. Moritz
places.note: Founded 1906: 21 rooms of Engadine furnishings, weapons and art from the 15th to 19th centuries. CHF 15, under-16s free. Closed 19 October to 5 December 2026, then Thursday to Sunday 11:00 to 17:00.

outings.why: Cog railway from Kleine Scheidegg through nine kilometres of tunnel inside the Eiger to 3,454m, for an ice palace, a glacier terrace and the Aletsch. It is a building, not a walk, and it is the single biggest expense of the trip.
outings.name: The Jungfraujoch
outings.season: All year. First train only, and only on a clear forecast.
outings.fallback: Männlichen to Kleine Scheidegg on foot, four hours and about CHF 40, with the same three faces and none of the queue.

outings.why: Cableway to Piz Gloria at 2,970m for the Thrill Walk at Birg, then ride down to Mürren and walk the contour path round to Gimmelwald under the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. About 400m of climbing on the walk.
outings.name: The Schilthorn and the Northface Trail
outings.season: Lifts all year. The Northface Trail mid-June to October.
outings.fallback: Mürren to Gimmelwald and back on the lower path, two hours, and skip the summit if it is sitting in cloud.

outings.why: Sixteen kilometres of ridge at around 2,300m between two mountain railways, over the Faulhorn at 2,681m, with the Jungfrau chain opposite all day and about 1,100m of climbing. The longest good day in the Oberland.
outings.name: Schynige Platte to First over the Faulhorn
outings.season: Early July to early October. Snow lingers on north slopes.
outings.fallback: Schynige Platte, the alpine garden and the Panoramaweg loop, three hours, and the cog railway back down.

outings.why: Six kilometres along the base of the north face from Eigergletscher station down to Alpiglen, 600m of descent on good path, with rockfall audible a few hundred metres above you most of the afternoon.
outings.name: The Eiger Trail
outings.season: Late June to mid-October.
outings.fallback: Kleine Scheidegg round to Alpiglen on the lower path, two hours, which works in cloud.

outings.why: The 1898 cog railway to 3,089m, then walk back down past the Riffelsee, which mirrors the Matterhorn if you are there before nine. CHF 132 return in summer, CHF 66 with a Swiss Travel Pass or Half Fare Card.
outings.name: The Gornergrat and the Riffelsee
outings.season: All year. The walk down is clear of snow from late June.
outings.fallback: Ride both ways and walk the ten minutes to the Riffelsee from Rotenboden, two hours in total.

outings.why: Seven hours and 1,250m of climbing from the village to a meadow terrace at 2,700m directly under the Matterhorn's north face, out through the Trift gorge and back by Zmutt. The best hard day in Zermatt and free.
outings.name: The Höhbalmen and Trift loop
outings.season: July to early October.
outings.fallback: Zermatt to Zmutt and back for lunch, three hours on a track, about 400m of climbing.

outings.why: Nine and a half kilometres and 400m down past Stellisee, Grindjisee, Grünsee, Moosjisee and Leisee, two of which hold the reflection. Easy underfoot, busy from mid-morning, and no Swiss Travel Pass discount on these lifts.
outings.name: The 5-Seenweg, Blauherd to Sunnegga
outings.season: Mid-June to mid-October.
outings.fallback: Sunnegga to Leisee and Findeln for lunch at Chez Vrony, three hours, mostly downhill.

outings.why: Cable cars to 3,883m, an ice palace inside the glacier and a view across into Italy. You gain 2,300m in forty minutes, which is why a third of the people up there have a headache.
outings.name: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise
outings.season: All year. Shuts for maintenance weeks in spring and autumn.
outings.fallback: Sunnegga and the Leisee for the afternoon when the top is closed for wind, which happens often.

outings.why: The largest glacier in the Alps seen first from the Eggishorn at 2,869m, then walked alongside on the ridge from Moosfluh to the Bettmerhorn. Seven kilometres at 2,300m with no shade and no water on the route.
outings.name: The Aletsch: Eggishorn to Bettmerhorn
outings.season: Lifts mid-June to late October. Ridge path from July.
outings.fallback: The Aletschwald from Riederfurka, three level hours in old pines, when the ridge is in cloud.

outings.why: Two hundred and ninety-one kilometres, 291 bridges and the Oberalp pass at 2,033m, in eight hours at an average of 39km/h. Covered by the Swiss Travel Pass apart from the compulsory seat reservation.
outings.name: The Glacier Express, Zermatt to St. Moritz
outings.season: Mid-December to mid-October. No trains mid-Oct to mid-Dec.
outings.fallback: The same route on ordinary regional trains, changing at Andermatt and Chur, with no reservation and half the fare.

outings.why: The highest rail crossing of the Alps without a rack rail, 2,253m at Ospizio Bernina, then 1,800m down past the Brusio spiral into Italy. Regional trains are covered by the Swiss Travel Pass; the panoramic one is not.
outings.name: The Bernina line to Alp Grüm and Tirano
outings.season: All year. Winter is the better half of it.
outings.fallback: Ospizio Bernina and Alp Grüm and back, four hours, if you would rather not cross the border.

outings.why: Paddle steamer down the lake to Vitznau, the 1871 cog railway to 1,798m, the panorama path round to Kaltbad, and down the far side to Arth-Goldau. All of it fully covered by the Swiss Travel Pass.
outings.name: Rigi Kulm by steamer and cog railway
outings.season: All year. The summit paths are clear May to November.
outings.fallback: Kaltbad, the Botta mineral baths and the panorama path, if the summit is inside a cloud.

outings.why: Boat to Alpnachstad, the 48 per cent cog railway to 2,128m, and cable cars down to Kriens. About CHF 122 full fare and half that with a Swiss Travel Pass.
outings.name: Mount Pilatus, the golden round trip
outings.season: Cog railway May to mid-November. Cableway all year.
outings.fallback: Up and down from Kriens by cable car, four hours, which is the winter version of this day anyway.

outings.why: Three hours by 1900s paddle steamer into the Urnersee, off at the meadow where the confederation was sworn in 1291, then the shore path on to Bauen or Brunnen. Free with the Swiss Travel Pass.
outings.name: The steamer to Rütli and the Weg der Schweiz
outings.season: Boats all year, most sailings May to October.
outings.fallback: Lucerne to Weggis and back on the boat, two hours, with lunch on deck.

outings.why: Eleven kilometres through UNESCO-listed vineyard terraces above Lac Léman, finishing in a village with two good cellars. Trains run back from every second village and there is no shade on any of it.
outings.name: The Lavaux terraces, Lutry to St-Saphorin
outings.season: April to late October. Harvest is late September.
outings.fallback: Lutry to Épesses only, two hours, and the train back from there.

outings.why: Cable car to 1,640m, down through the Wildkirchli caves to the inn built against the cliff, then over and down to a lake under the Säntis wall. Six hundred metres of descent on stone steps and tree roots.
outings.name: Ebenalp, the Äscher and the Seealpsee
outings.season: Lifts and the mountain inns roughly May to late October.
outings.fallback: Wasserauen to the Seealpsee and back on the farm road, three hours, no lift and no exposure.

outings.why: Three Milanese castles on one hillside in the morning, CHF 10 for all of them, then up the Verzasca to the Ponte dei Salti at Lavertezzo and the stone village of Corippo in the afternoon.
outings.name: Bellinzona's castles and the Val Verzasca
outings.season: All year. The river is only swimmable July to September.
outings.fallback: The castles and a long lunch in Bellinzona, then the train back, if the valley bus times do not work.

outings.why: Three passes above 2,100m in a day by car or postbus, taking in the Rhône glacier ice grotto on the Furka. All three are shut by snow for about seven months of the year and there is no way round that.
outings.name: The Furka, Grimsel and Susten pass loop
outings.season: Roughly mid-June to late October. Snow-closed otherwise.
outings.fallback: The Schöllenen gorge and the Devil's Bridge, then the Furka steam railway to Oberwald, if the passes are shut.

outings.why: Six kilometres of arcade, a 100m spire with 344 steps, eleven 16th-century fountains, and the river the whole city swims in from June. Flat, compact, and it rains here more than it does in Zürich.
outings.name: Bern on foot: the Lauben, the Münster and the Aare
outings.season: All year. The river swim June to early September.
outings.fallback: Zentrum Paul Klee and the Kunstmuseum back to back in the wet, both minutes from the station.

outings.why: Grossmünster and the Chagall windows before ten, the Kunsthaus or the Landesmuseum after, the Viadukt in Zürich West for lunch, and a lake swim at Utoquai in summer. All of it inside one tram zone.
outings.name: Zürich on foot: the Altstadt, the Kunsthaus and the lake
outings.season: All year. The lake baths mid-May to mid-September.
outings.fallback: Landesmuseum and the Kunsthaus, both indoors and fifteen minutes apart, then the Niederdorf for dinner.

sources: 2026-10-29 repair: meals, places and hours added from venue menus and Wanderlog place pages; CHF at 1.2073 USD (30rates.com, 28 Oct 2026)

destination.name: Switzerland: the Oberland, Zermatt, the Engadin and Ticino
destination.pitch: The mountains are the trip and the towns are only the beds: the Jungfraujoch, the Gornergrat, the Aletsch and two named rail lines, joined by the best public transport on earth, at a price that will startle you daily.
destination.caveat: The money: CHF 32 for rösti, CHF 132 to the Gornergrat, CHF 240 to the Jungfraujoch, and a six-day Swiss Travel Pass at CHF 399. From mid-April to mid-June and mid-October to mid-December most lifts and half the hotels in Zermatt and Grindelwald are shut. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Zürich is a real city for two nights and Bern is a better one to walk. Neither is why you came, and after four days in the mountains both feel like a detour.
because.food: Narrow and done properly rather than broad: alp cheese, dried meat, lake perch, Ticino merlot and a Chasselas that never leaves the country. Restaurant prices are the highest in Europe and the markets are the answer.
because.nature: The Aletsch is the largest glacier in the Alps and you can walk beside it for seven kilometres; Lauterbrunnen has 72 waterfalls between vertical walls; and all of it is reachable without a car.
because.culture: Four thousand Klees in Bern, the world's largest Giacometti holding in Zürich, Segantini's Alpine triptych above St. Moritz, and an Appenzell assembly that still votes by show of hands.
because.adventure: Via ferratas, the Höhbalmen and Faulhorn ridge days, a 220m bungee off the Verzasca dam, and glacier routes that need a rope and a guide and say so on the sign.
because.relaxation: Lake swimming from mid-June, a Botta bath house on a shelf above Lake Lucerne, and car-free villages where the loudest thing is a cog railway. Doing nothing here is expensive and very good.
because.exploration: Four languages inside 350 kilometres, and the interest is how they hold together: a Reformation pulpit in Zürich, a Milanese castle in Bellinzona, a Romansh national park in the east.
